chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad, from Sahl ibn Ziyad and Ishaq ibn Muhammad and others besides them, raising it [with an elevated chain], he said:

The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) was seated in Kufa after his return from [the battle of] Siffeen, when an old man came forward and knelt before him, then said to him: 'O Commander of the Faithful! Inform us about our march to the people of Syria — was it by an ordainment from God and pre-determination?' So the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes, O Shaykh! You did not ascend any hill nor descend into any valley except by an ordainment from God and pre-determination.'

So the Shaykh said to him: 'Will my exhaustion be counted [as reward] with God, O Commander of the Faithful?' So he said to him: 'Shh! O Shaykh! By God, God has magnified the reward for your travels while you were traveling, and for your staying while you were staying, and for your departure while you were departing, and you were not in any of your states being coerced nor compelled to it.'

So the Shaykh said to him: 'And how were we not in any of our states being coerced nor compelled to it, when our march, our return, and our departure were by ordainment and pre-determination?' So he said to him: 'Do you think it was an unavoidable ordainment and a necessitated pre-determination? If it were so, reward and punishment would be invalidated, as would commanding [good] and forbidding [evil] and rebuke from God, and the meaning of promise and threat would crumble. Then no sinner would be blameworthy nor any good-doer praiseworthy, and the sinner would be more deserving of good treatment than the good-doer, and the good-doer would be more deserving of punishment than the sinner. That is the statement of the brothers of idol-worshippers, and the opponents of the All-Merciful, and the party of Satan, and the Qadariyya of this community and its Magians.'

'Indeed, God — Blessed and Exalted — imposed obligations through [man's] choice, and forbade [things] as a warning, and gives much for a little [deed], and is not disobeyed by being overpowered, and is not obeyed by compulsion, and did not give control as a delegation [of authority], and did not create the heavens and the earth and what is between them in vain, and did not send the Prophets as bearers of glad tidings and warners in futility. That is the conjecture of those who disbelieve. So woe to those who disbelieve from the Fire!'

Then the Shaykh began to say [in verse]: 'You are the Imam through whose obedience we hope / On the Day of Salvation for forgiveness from the All-Merciful. You have clarified from our matters what was obscure / May your Lord recompense you with excellence for your excellence.'

key_terms.الأمر بين الأمرين: The matter between two matters — the Shia theological position between absolute determinism (jabr) and absolute delegation (tafwid)
key_terms.التفويض: Delegation/indeterminism — the view that God has delegated all actions to humans, also rejected
key_terms.الجبر: Compulsion/determinism — the view that humans have no free will, rejected here
key_terms.القدرية: The Qadariyya — early Islamic theological faction holding views on fate and free will
key_terms.القضاء والقدر: Divine ordainment and pre-determination; the theological concepts of God's decree and measure
key_terms.مجوس: Magians/Zoroastrians — used here metaphorically for those whose theology resembles dualist determinism

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Ali say about divine decree (qada and qadar) and human free will?
ai.summary: This famous hadith narrates a dialogue between Imam Ali (AS) and an old man in Kufa shortly after the Battle of Siffeen (37 AH/657 CE). The man asks whether their campaign against the Syrians was divinely ordained and pre-determined. Imam Ali confirms that divine decree encompasses every movement, but crucially distinguishes between determinism (jabr) and free will: God's decree does not compel humans or negate their moral responsibility. The Imam refutes the fatalist position by showing that absolute determinism would destroy the foundations of morality, divine justice, and prophethood itself. This hadith is a cornerstone of Shia theology on the matter of 'al-amr bayn al-amrayn' — the middle position between compulsion and delegation.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Muhammad, from Sahl Bin Ziyad and Is’haq Bin Muhammad and someone else, raising it,

He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> was seated in Al-Kufa, after his<sup>asws</sup> leaving from (the battle of) Siffeen, when an old man squatted in front of him<sup>asws</sup>, then said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘O Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup>! Inform us about our travel to the people of Syria. Was it by an Ordainment from Allah<sup>azwj</sup> and Pre-determination?’ So Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Yes O Sheykh! No hill did you ascend nor a valley you descend into except it was by an Ordainment from Allah<sup>azwj</sup> and Pre-determined’.

So the Sheykh said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘Will my exhaustion be Counted in the Presence of Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, O Amir Al Momineen<sup>asws</sup>?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said to him: ‘Muh! (Shh!), O Sheykh! Allah<sup>azwj</sup> has Magnified the Recompense regarding your travels while you were travelling, and regarding your staying while you were staying, and regarding your leaving, while you were leaving, and you did not happen to be in anything from your states being coerced nor forced to it’.

So the Sheykh said to him, ‘And how can it be that we were not in anything from our states being coerced nor being forced to it, and it was with the Ordainment and the Pre-determination, our travels, and our transfers, and our leaving?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said to him: ‘And you think that it was an unavoidable Ordainment, Necessitated? If it was like that, it would invalidate the Rewards, and the Punishments, and the enjoinment, and the forbiddance, and the Rebukes from Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, the meanings of the Promises and the Threats would crumble. 
So the sinners would not be blameable nor would the good doers be praiseworthy. It would have been so that the sinner would be closer with the good deed than the good doer, and it would be so that the good doer would be closer with the Punishment than the sinner. These are the talks of the brotherhood of the idol-worshippers, and the disputants to the Beneficent, and parties of the Satan<sup>la</sup>, and the Qadiriyya of this community and its Magians.

Surely, Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Blessed and High Encumbered choices and Forbade as a warning, and Gives a lot upon the little (deed), and He<sup>azwj</sup> is not disobeyed due to being overcome, nor is He<sup>azwj</sup> obeyed forcefully, and did not Give control as a delegated (authority), and did not Create the skies and the earth and what is between the two in vain, and did not Send the Prophets<sup>as</sup>, the Givers of Glad Tidings and the Warners in futility. That is a conjecture of those who are disbelieving. So woe be unto those who are disbelieving of the Fire!’

So the Sheykh prosed saying, ‘You<sup>asws</sup> are the Imam<sup>asws</sup> whom we are hoping to by obeying him<sup>asws</sup> on a Day for salvation from the Beneficent (and for) Forgiveness. You<sup>asws</sup> clarified from our matters what was vague. May your<sup>asws</sup> Lord<sup>azwj</sup> Recompense you by a Favour with the favour’.
